test_title: PYST 63: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held On 28 Jun, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following is an INCORRECTLY stated social impact of the Green Revolution?

options.text: Primarily, the medium and large farmers were benefited
Worsened the condition of landless and marginal farmers
Only farmers involved in subsistence agriculture were benefitted
There was displacement of service caste group

solution:
The correct answer is __**Only farmers involved in subsistence agriculture were benefitted**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Only farmers involved in subsistence agriculture were benefitted** is an incorrect statement regarding the social impact of the Green Revolution.
 
• The Green Revolution primarily benefited medium and large-scale farmers who had the resources to invest in new technologies.
 
• It worsened the condition of landless and marginal farmers who could not compete with the increased productivity of larger farms.
 
• Service caste groups were displaced as traditional agricultural practices and labor requirements changed.
 
• The Green Revolution led to increased disparities in income and land ownership, favoring those who were already better off.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Green Revolution refers to a set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that took place between the 1940s and the late 1960s, which increased agricultural production worldwide, particularly in developing countries.
 
• Key elements included the development of high-yielding varieties of cereal grains, expansion of irrigation infrastructure, modernization of management techniques, distribution of hybridized seeds, synthetic fertilizers, and pesticides to farmers.
 
• While it significantly increased food production and reduced hunger, it also led to social and economic inequalities and environmental issues such as soil degradation and pesticide contamination.
 
• The Green Revolution is often credited with helping to avoid widespread famine and feeding millions of people, but its benefits were not uniformly distributed across all segments of the population.
